sources.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

inputs.question: What did Jesus say when Peter asked how many times he should forgive?

answer: Peter asked whether he should forgive his brother “until seven times,” and Jesus answered, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven” [S1]. Jesus’ answer goes far beyond the number Peter proposed [S1].

sources.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness. God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.

inputs.question: What happened on the first day of creation?

answer: On the first day God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light [S1]. God saw that the light was good, divided the light from the darkness, and called the light “day” and the darkness “night” [S1]. The passage closes with “There was evening and there was morning, the first day” [S1].

sources.text: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.

inputs.question: What did Ruth say to Naomi when Naomi urged her to go back?

answer: Ruth refused to leave. She said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God” [S1]. Her words commit her not only to Naomi but also to Naomi’s people and to Naomi’s God [S1].

sources.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

answer: John 3:16 says: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life” [S1]. The verse links God’s love for the world with the giving of his Son, and promises eternal life to whoever believes in him [S1].

sources.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

answer: Psalm 23 begins, “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing” [S1]. The opening lines continue the shepherd picture: he makes the psalmist lie down in green pastures, leads him beside still waters, restores his soul and guides him “in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake” [S1].
